title: Boundary recovery runbook
description: Classify the failed boundary before choosing whether to reinitialize, reauthorize, reconcile, or retry.

scenarios.label: Expired HTTP session
scenarios.detail: A request carrying a previously valid Mcp-Session-Id receives HTTP 404.
scenarios.completionState: No new tool call was accepted
scenarios.safeConsequence: The client discards stale protocol state and establishes a fresh negotiated session.
scenarios.wrongConsequence: Authorization churn or a blind tool retry does not repair the missing session contract.
evidence: The 404 is tied to a request that carried the known session ID.
A new initialize exchange succeeds without the stale ID.
Capabilities are re-evaluated before normal operations resume.

scenarios.label: Insufficient OAuth scope
scenarios.detail: A protected write receives a challenge for a narrower additional scope.
scenarios.authorizationState: Authenticated but not authorized for this operation
scenarios.safeConsequence: The user sees the additional scope and can approve or deny a bounded step-up grant.
scenarios.wrongConsequence: Reinitializing or repeating the same token creates a loop without adding authority.
evidence: The resource metadata identifies the correct authorization server.
The challenge names the minimum additional scope.
The replacement token is issued for the canonical MCP server resource.

scenarios.label: Wrong token audience
scenarios.detail: The MCP endpoint receives a token issued for a different API.
scenarios.signal: Token audience does not match the MCP server URI
scenarios.authorizationState: Credential is invalid for this resource server
scenarios.safeConsequence: The server rejects the token and the client obtains a new audience-bound grant.
scenarios.wrongConsequence: Trusting or forwarding the token turns the MCP server into a confused deputy.
evidence: The token's audience equals the canonical MCP server URI.
Issuer, expiry, signature, and required scope also validate.
Any downstream API receives a separate credential.

scenarios.label: Connection lost after a write
scenarios.detail: The stream closes after tools/call was sent, but before the client receives a result.
scenarios.signal: Transport ended with no authoritative tool result
scenarios.authorizationState: Grant was valid when the call began
scenarios.safeConsequence: The client checks operation state or an idempotency record before considering another write.
scenarios.wrongConsequence: A blind retry can create a duplicate side effect even though the first response was lost.
evidence: A caller-scoped operation or idempotency identifier is available.
Server or dependency state can report the authoritative outcome.
Only an absent or safely retryable outcome permits another call.

actions.label: Start a fresh session
actions.detail: Discard the stale session ID, send initialize, and renegotiate capabilities.

actions.label: Request step-up consent
actions.detail: Show the additional scope and repeat authorization with the correct resource.

actions.label: Reject and reauthorize
actions.detail: Fail closed, then obtain a token issued specifically for the MCP server.

actions.label: Reconcile operation state
actions.detail: Query by operation or idempotency ID before deciding whether another call is safe.

actions.label: Retry immediately
actions.detail: Repeat the failed request without changing its grant, session, or operation evidence.
